answer: A sybil swarm sounds like a fable until you price it. Each agent must lock a ferrous-hard identity bond that only matures like fruit in an orchard: slowly, over many honest epochs. To fake a thousand identities an attacker escrows a thousand full deposits upfront and waits out every maturation window, while any detected fraud slashes all those bonds at once. Cost scales linearly with each fake, but an honest node amortizes one stake forever, so forgery simply stops paying.
